question: The Commission has issued recommendations on the protection of journalists and other media professionals in the EU, namely Recommendations (EU) 2021/15341 and (EU) 2022/7582. The Mass-Media Forum took place in Chisinau, Moldova, on 8 December 2025. Press representatives, media experts and other relevant stakeholders participated.

I received reports from Moldova that representatives of independent media organisations that are more critical of the government were not allowed into the room. The reason given was that ‘there were no more seats available in the room’, although photographs show that there was still plenty of room. This gives the impression that media pluralism is being undermined.
According to its website, the Mass-Media Forum is co-sponsored by the European Union3. 1.
Is the Commission aware of these worrying signs?
Does the Commission intend to continue providing financial support to the Mass-Media Forum?

Can the Commission indicate whether respect for press and media freedom is one of the conditions for becoming a candidate country, and whether violations of this freedom could constitute grounds for (temporarily) suspending accession negotiations?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (1.4.2026) On 8 December 2025 in Chisinau, the Media Forum organised an activity of the Building Resilience in Moldova project funded by the EU and implemented by the Institute for War and Peace Reporting in partnership with the Association of Independent Press.

Those wishing to participate in the Forum were required to register in advance, with seats allocated through an online registration system. Guaranteeing freedom of expression and media freedom is a fundamental requirement that candidate countries applying for EU membership are required to meet as part of the enlargement process.

The EU has put in place several initiatives which support and protect independent media and journalists1. These are now part of the EU acquis that candidate countries must align with as part of the EU accession process.

The Commission will continue to monitor freedom of expression in Moldova both in terms of alignment with the EU acquis and in terms of providing adequate protection for journalists against all forms of intimidation and attacks.
1 Commission Recommendation (EU) 2021/1534 of 16 September 2021 on ensuring the protection, safety and

empowerment of journalists and other media professionals in the European Union: https://eurlex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX:32021H1534; Commission Recommendation (EU) 2022/758 of 27 April 2022 on protecting journalists and human rights defenders who engage in public participation: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reco/2022/758/oj/eng; Regulation (EU) 2024/1083 of 11 April 2024 on European Media Freedom Act: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1083/oj/eng.
